metadata_candidate.title: Agreeableness: cooperation, candor, and interpersonal boundaries
metadata_candidate.description: Consider trust, straightforwardness, altruism, compliance, modesty, and tender-mindedness without treating cooperation as virtue or disagreement as defect.

metadata_candidate.title: High agreeableness: supporting cooperation without erasing your boundaries
metadata_candidate.description: A high agreeableness result suggests frequent compassion, respectful restraint, or willingness to trust and cooperate; it does not measure kindness, morality, weakness, or relationship success.

metadata_candidate.title: Low agreeableness: using skepticism and directness without contempt
metadata_candidate.description: A low agreeableness result suggests less frequent accommodation, trusting assumptions, or compassionate restraint; it does not mean cruel, dishonest, unsafe, selfish, or incapable of care.

metadata_candidate.title: Middle agreeableness: adjusting cooperation to evidence and relationship
metadata_candidate.description: A middle agreeableness result is a selective cooperation pattern, not an absence of character: trust, accommodation, and directness may shift with evidence, stakes, reciprocity, and role.

metadata_candidate.title: Conscientiousness: structure, follow-through, and adaptive effort
metadata_candidate.description: Explore how planning and persistence can help or hinder depending on risk, timing, and flexibility across six narrower facets.

metadata_candidate.title: High conscientiousness: creating dependable structure without overloading it
metadata_candidate.description: A high conscientiousness result suggests a frequent preference for organization, reliable effort, and honoring commitments; it does not measure worth, diligence in every setting, or guaranteed performance.

metadata_candidate.title: Low conscientiousness: building support without turning the score into blame
metadata_candidate.description: A low conscientiousness result suggests a weaker or less consistent preference for order, sustained routines, and obligation tracking; it does not mean lazy, selfish, incapable, or beyond change.

metadata_candidate.title: Middle conscientiousness: scaling structure to consequence and capacity
metadata_candidate.description: A middle conscientiousness result is a selective control pattern, not an absence of character: structure may increase with consequence, ownership, or coordination needs and relax elsewhere.

metadata_candidate.title: Emotional stability protocol: add deliberate early warning to a steady response
metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is a steady-response and early-warning protocol: preserve calm while checking external indicators, affected people, accumulating load, and a scheduled review point.

metadata_candidate.title: Extraversion: social energy, participation, and stimulation
metadata_candidate.description: Examine how warmth, group seeking, assertiveness, pace, stimulation, and positive emotion may combine without equating quietness with shyness or leadership ability.

metadata_candidate.title: High extraversion: creating momentum while leaving room for other voices
metadata_candidate.description: A high extraversion result suggests frequent social approach, visible initiative, or energetic engagement; it does not measure confidence, social skill, happiness, popularity, or leadership ability.

metadata_candidate.title: Low extraversion: contributing with lower stimulation and deliberate visibility
metadata_candidate.description: A low extraversion result suggests less frequent social approach, outward assertiveness, or high activation; it does not mean shy, anxious, unfriendly, passive, unconfident, or unable to lead.

metadata_candidate.title: Middle extraversion: adjusting participation to purpose and stimulation
metadata_candidate.description: A middle extraversion result is a selective engagement pattern, not a lack of personality: approach, assertiveness, and activation may rise with purpose, familiarity, or role and recede elsewhere.

metadata_candidate.title: Big Five facets: a 30-facet map within five domains
metadata_candidate.description: Browse thirty narrower Big Five facets under their five parent domains, and use each link as an observation prompt rather than a diagnosis, rank, or fixed identity.

metadata_candidate.title: Achievement striving facet: setting and pursuing demanding aims
metadata_candidate.description: Achievement striving describes a narrower conscientiousness tendency to set demanding standards and invest effort toward advancement; it is not talent, status, productivity, or a requirement to maximize every goal.

metadata_candidate.title: Actions facet: willingness to vary routines and try unfamiliar activity
metadata_candidate.description: Actions describes a narrower openness tendency toward trying unfamiliar activities and varying established routines; it is not impulsiveness, courage, travel frequency, or risk tolerance.

metadata_candidate.title: Activity facet: preferring a busy pace and sustained movement
metadata_candidate.description: Activity describes a narrower extraversion tendency toward a full schedule, quick tempo, and ongoing engagement; it is not health, productivity, attention capacity, or superior time management.

metadata_candidate.title: Aesthetics facet: noticing form, beauty, and sensory composition
metadata_candidate.description: Aesthetics describes a narrower openness tendency to notice and value form, beauty, artistic expression, or sensory composition; it is not artistic skill or superior taste.

metadata_candidate.title: Altruism facet: noticing and acting on opportunities to help
metadata_candidate.description: Altruism describes a narrower agreeableness tendency to offer time, effort, or resources for another person's benefit; it is not moral worth, unlimited self-sacrifice, effectiveness, or consent to exploitation.

metadata_candidate.title: Anger facet: how readily frustration becomes an angry response
metadata_candidate.description: Anger is a narrow neuroticism facet about the tendency for obstruction, unfairness, or disrespect to evoke irritation or anger; it does not measure aggression, violence, moral character, or whether a complaint is justified.

metadata_candidate.title: Anxiety facet: anticipating possible trouble without making a diagnosis
metadata_candidate.description: Anxiety is a narrow neuroticism facet describing how readily attention turns toward possible danger, uncertainty, or things that could go wrong; the label is not an anxiety-disorder diagnosis or a measure of courage.

metadata_candidate.title: Assertiveness facet: taking the floor and influencing direction
metadata_candidate.description: Assertiveness describes a narrower extraversion tendency to speak up, state preferences, and influence group direction; it is not correctness, aggression, confidence in every domain, or leadership quality.

metadata_candidate.title: Competence facet: approaching tasks with workable confidence
metadata_candidate.description: Competence describes a narrower conscientiousness tendency to expect that one can understand, organize, and handle ordinary demands; it is not a verified skill score or a guarantee of performance.

metadata_candidate.title: Compliance facet: de-escalating conflict without erasing disagreement
metadata_candidate.description: Compliance describes a narrower agreeableness tendency to yield, compromise, or reduce confrontation during conflict; it is not obedience, consent, weakness, conflict skill, or acceptance of harm.

metadata_candidate.title: Deliberation facet: pausing to consider consequences before action
metadata_candidate.description: Deliberation describes a narrower conscientiousness tendency to examine options and likely consequences before acting; it is not intelligence, fearfulness, indecision, or proof that a choice will be correct.

metadata_candidate.title: Depression facet: proneness to discouragement, not a clinical diagnosis
metadata_candidate.description: Depression is a legacy facet label for a tendency toward discouragement, sadness, or diminished positive expectation; on this page it is a personality-navigation term, not a diagnosis of depressive disorder or an estimate of mental-health severity.

metadata_candidate.title: Dutifulness facet: responding to obligations and agreed rules
metadata_candidate.description: Dutifulness describes a narrower conscientiousness tendency to take promises, roles, and agreed standards seriously; it is not a measure of moral worth, obedience, or whether a rule is legitimate.

metadata_candidate.title: Excitement seeking facet: preferring intensity and stimulation
metadata_candidate.description: Excitement seeking describes a narrower extraversion tendency to prefer vivid, fast, or high-stimulation experiences; it is not courage, recklessness, addiction, risk competence, or a need for danger.

metadata_candidate.title: Feelings facet: attending to and differentiating inner emotion
metadata_candidate.description: Feelings describes a narrower openness tendency to attend to, differentiate, and treat inner emotional experience as information; it is not empathy, stability, or emotional intensity alone.

metadata_candidate.title: Gregariousness facet: preferring company and group settings
metadata_candidate.description: Gregariousness describes a narrower extraversion preference for being with several people and entering group settings; it is not social skill, popularity, belonging, or protection from loneliness.

metadata_candidate.title: Ideas facet: appetite for concepts, questions, and abstract exploration
metadata_candidate.description: Ideas describes a narrower openness tendency toward intellectual curiosity, conceptual exploration, and unfamiliar questions; it is not intelligence, education, accuracy, or expertise.

metadata_candidate.title: Imagination facet: how readily you build inner possibilities
metadata_candidate.description: Imagination describes a narrower openness tendency toward mental imagery, hypothetical scenes, and internally generated possibilities; it is not the whole openness domain or a creativity score.

metadata_candidate.title: Impulsiveness facet: difficulty delaying an urge, not a diagnosis
metadata_candidate.description: Impulsiveness is a narrow neuroticism facet about how difficult it can feel to delay a strong urge when emotion or desire is active; it is not a diagnosis, a global measure of self-control, or proof of irresponsible behavior.

metadata_candidate.title: Modesty facet: limiting self-enhancement in social comparison
metadata_candidate.description: Modesty describes a narrower agreeableness tendency to avoid inflating one's importance or claiming excessive credit; it is not low self-esteem, low ability, silence, or refusal to document contribution.

metadata_candidate.title: Order facet: arranging materials, time, and routines
metadata_candidate.description: Order describes a narrower conscientiousness preference for structure, designated places, and predictable sequences; it is not cleanliness, moral discipline, or proof that a system works well.

metadata_candidate.title: Positive emotions facet: readily experiencing and expressing uplift
metadata_candidate.description: Positive emotions describes a narrower extraversion tendency toward frequent or readily expressed joy, enthusiasm, and amusement; it is not mental health, life satisfaction, optimism, or freedom from distress.

metadata_candidate.title: Self-consciousness facet: sensitivity to being observed or judged
metadata_candidate.description: Self-consciousness is a narrow neuroticism facet describing how readily attention turns inward when a person may be observed, evaluated, or embarrassed; it is not vanity, humility, social skill, or a diagnosis of social anxiety.

metadata_candidate.title: Self-discipline facet: continuing intended action through friction
metadata_candidate.description: Self-discipline describes a narrower conscientiousness tendency to begin and continue intended tasks despite boredom, distraction, or low immediate reward; it is not willpower purity, health, or constant productivity.

metadata_candidate.title: Straightforwardness facet: communicating without strategic distortion
metadata_candidate.description: Straightforwardness describes a narrower agreeableness tendency toward candid, non-manipulative communication; it is not saying everything, perfect accuracy, bluntness, or surrendering privacy.

metadata_candidate.title: Tender-mindedness facet: weighting compassion in judgment
metadata_candidate.description: Tender-mindedness describes a narrower agreeableness tendency to give emotional suffering and humane concern weight in decisions; it is not fragility, sentimentality, clinical empathy, or always choosing leniency.

metadata_candidate.title: Trust facet: starting from cooperative expectations with safeguards
metadata_candidate.description: Trust describes a narrower agreeableness tendency to expect that other people generally intend fair or cooperative interaction; it is not gullibility, safety, credibility, or proof about a specific person.

metadata_candidate.title: Values facet: willingness to examine and revise guiding assumptions
metadata_candidate.description: Values describes a narrower openness tendency to examine conventions and revise guiding assumptions when reasons or experience change; it is not morality, ideology, or lack of commitment.

metadata_candidate.title: Vulnerability facet: feeling overwhelmed under acute pressure
metadata_candidate.description: Vulnerability is a narrow neuroticism facet describing the tendency to feel less able to think or act effectively when pressure becomes intense; it is not fragility, trauma history, incapacity, or a prediction of performance.

metadata_candidate.title: Warmth facet: expressing interpersonal welcome and closeness
metadata_candidate.description: Warmth describes a narrower extraversion tendency to show friendliness, affection, and interpersonal welcome; it is not empathy, agreement, intimacy, or proof of caring behavior.

metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is a helping-boundary protocol for people whose cooperation has become hard to evaluate: map consent, ownership, reciprocity, capacity, and a clear stopping point.

metadata_candidate.title: High conscientiousness workload audit: protect commitments by reducing control debt
metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is a workload-audit protocol for people whose reliability systems have become crowded: inventory commitments, test control costs, reset standards, and preserve recovery capacity.

metadata_candidate.title: High extraversion interaction audit: budget social energy and shared airtime
metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is an interaction-budget protocol for people who create momentum through contact: map optional and essential exchanges, protect recovery, and redistribute speaking space.

metadata_candidate.title: High neuroticism signal audit: calibrate threat, action, and recovery
metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is a threat-signal and recovery audit: separate observable cues from interpretations, choose the minimum useful action, and close the monitoring loop when evidence permits.

metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is a minimum-viable-structure plan for a missed or drifting commitment: clarify the obligation, externalize one next action, shorten feedback, and renegotiate openly.

metadata_candidate.description: This legacy page is a quiet-participation protocol: identify the decision window, prepare one contribution, choose an accessible channel, request a turn, and protect recovery.

metadata_candidate.description: Use anxiety, anger, depression, self-consciousness, impulsiveness, and vulnerability as observation prompts without turning a trait result into a mental-health diagnosis.

metadata_candidate.title: High neuroticism: noticing emotional signals without letting them run the response
metadata_candidate.description: A high neuroticism result suggests more frequent worry, distress, frustration, or emotional fluctuation; it does not establish a disorder, fragility, poor judgment, or inability to recover.

metadata_candidate.title: Low neuroticism: using emotional steadiness without missing early signals
metadata_candidate.description: A low neuroticism result suggests less frequent distress, worry, or emotional fluctuation; it does not mean invulnerable, fearless, unaffected, always regulated, or certain to recover quickly.

metadata_candidate.title: Middle neuroticism: tracking when emotional reactivity rises or settles
metadata_candidate.description: A middle neuroticism result is a conditional reactivity pattern, not emotional blankness: sensitivity, activation, and recovery may shift with uncertainty, control, fatigue, stakes, and support.

metadata_candidate.title: Openness: how curiosity and familiarity can shape choices
metadata_candidate.description: Read openness as a continuous tendency toward ideas, imagination, aesthetics, feelings, varied actions, and reconsidered values—not as a measure of intelligence or creativity.

metadata_candidate.title: High openness: exploring widely and choosing deliberately
metadata_candidate.description: A high openness result suggests frequent engagement with ideas, imagination, aesthetics, feelings, varied actions, or reconsidered assumptions; it does not rank intelligence or creativity.

metadata_candidate.title: Low openness: using stable methods and testing change by evidence
metadata_candidate.description: A low openness result suggests a stronger preference for familiar, concrete, or proven approaches in many situations; it does not mean unintelligent, unimaginative, or incapable of change.

metadata_candidate.title: Middle openness: changing the exploration threshold by context
metadata_candidate.description: A middle openness result is a selective pattern, not an absence of personality: you may explore when the expected value clears a context-dependent threshold and preserve familiar methods elsewhere.

metadata_candidate.title: 神经质较低：运用情绪稳定，也不漏掉早期信号
metadata_candidate.description: 神经质较低表示痛苦、担忧或情绪波动可能较少出现，但不代表不会受伤、毫无恐惧、不受影响、调节永远有效或必然快速恢复。

metadata_candidate.title: 神经质中间区间：追踪情绪反应何时升高、何时平复
metadata_candidate.description: 中间区间具有明确的条件性反应模式：敏感度、激活程度与恢复速度会随不确定性、控制感、疲劳、后果和支持变化，呈现可识别条件。

metadata_candidate.title: 开放性：在新可能与熟悉经验之间怎样选择
metadata_candidate.description: 从想象、审美、感受、行动、观念与价值六个侧面观察对新经验的接近方式，不把开放性等同于聪明、创意或见识。

metadata_candidate.title: 开放性较高：扩大探索，也给选择设置停止条件
metadata_candidate.description: 开放性较高表示更常接近观念、想象、审美、感受、多样行动或对既有假设的复查，但不代表智力、创意或见识等级。

metadata_candidate.title: 开放性较低：保护稳定，也用证据决定何时改变
metadata_candidate.description: 开放性较低表示在许多情境中更偏好熟悉、具体或经过验证的做法，但不代表智力低、没有想象力或无法改变。

metadata_candidate.title: 开放性中间区间：根据情境调整探索门槛
metadata_candidate.description: 中间区间具有明确的选择性模式：当新方案的预期价值超过情境门槛时扩大选项，在其他任务中保留熟悉做法。

metadata_candidate.title: 大五人格来源、复审与纠错政策
metadata_candidate.description: 说明来源如何分类、映射主张、接受复审与纠错，并与竞品观察或无证据产品主张保持分离。

metadata_candidate.title: 大五人格测试：测什么，以及怎样使用报告
metadata_candidate.description: 这项自陈测评把回答组织为开放性、尽责性、外倾性、宜人性和神经质五个宽泛维度。结果适合用作可检验的反思假设，不是诊断、固定身份或资格判断。

metadata_candidate.title: 大五人格：模型、结果与实践反思
metadata_candidate.description: 按问题浏览 backend-authoritative 的大五人格内容：理解模型、谨慎阅读结果、检验具体行动，或查看证据与限制。
